title: Introduce column-gesture preview and density spectra for virtualized table
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table performs well but users struggle with column resizing feedback, unexpected layout shifts, and unclear density controls. Current interactions are brittle when rows are continuously mounted/unmounted during drag, and accessibility announces noisy intermediate widths.

Goal: Design an interaction pattern ("column-gesture preview") that gives immediate visual feedback without causing layout thrash, pairs with a 'density spectra' token mapping so users can discover compact/comfortable modes, and works with virtualization, keyboard, and screen reader flows. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens, an accessibility spec, acceptance criteria, and a lightweight interaction prototype for engineering to validate perf impact.
background: Recent support tickets call out: columns appearing to 'jump' during drag (esp. with large datasets), inconsistent snap behavior across density settings, and confusing keyboard resize semantics. Engineering telemetry shows many column-resize events spike reflows. Design tokens for spacing/density currently live in tokens.table.* but lack a mapped preview state for intermediate densities. This ticket bridges tokens, micro-interaction, and virtualization constraints.
user_personas: Product manager exploring large dataset views (needs predictable column widths)
Data analyst toggling density to fit more rows on screen
Developer embedding Redwood table component into a dashboard (concerned with perf)
Screen reader user navigating table column controls
constraints: Must not increase per-frame JS work that causes >16ms frames on target client hardware
Should work with our virtualization strategy (row recycling + prefetch window)
Must be keyboard-accessible and limit aria noise to final commit of changes
Dense mode needs token-driven spacing so we can expose a compact preset
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight overlay layer when user begins a column drag: the overlay shows a semi-transparent preview of new column boundaries and a live width tooltip; actual DOM column widths are not committed until drag end to avoid repeated layout invalidation
Snaplines: compute snap thresholds client-side using stable heuristics (min width, content priority token), show soft-snap (magnetic) feedback in preview, and apply hard snap at commit

Density spectra: expose a horizontal mini-panel inside the table header that previews density token mapping (comfort -> balanced -> compact). Changing spectrum updates preview tokens without remounting rows; commit applies token and triggers a single reconciliation pass
Keyboard flow: left/right arrow with modifier increases/decreases width in 8px steps, preview announced once with live region summarizing 'Column width preview: 120px — press Enter to apply'

Accessibility: reduce aria-live chatter by making the preview announcements polite and only announce final width on commit; provide an alternative 'immediate apply' setting for users who prefer real-time changes
Engineering hooks: provide a minimal event contract (onResizePreviewStart, onResizePreviewUpdate, onResizeCommit) and a toggle to disable overlay for legacy clients
design_decisions: Commit-only resize to avoid layout thrash: preview versus commit separated intentionally to reduce reflow overhead
Preview overlay drawn in a fixed-position canvas sibling to table DOM to avoid triggering table layout during drag
Density is token-driven (tokens.table.rowGap/rowPadding/compactMultiplier) rather than ad-hoc CSS classes so we can offer consistent metrics across components
acceptance_criteria: Preview overlay appears immediately on drag start and tracks pointer without changing committed column widths
Final column widths commit on drag end and persist to layout state
Keyboard resize flow mirrors pointer flow and is fully operable with screen readers
Changing density via spectrum panel updates preview tokens without unmounting rows; commit applies tokens and results in single reconciliation pass
Telemetry events emitted for preview start/update/commit and flagged in ENG-1984 for perf review
Design tokens and documentation published to tokens.table.* and design-system-2026.03 release notes include migration guidance

risks: If overlay approach is mis-implemented, desktop browsers with compositing limits might still show jank — mitigated via engineering spike
Screen reader users may prefer immediate applies; we must offer a preference and test widely
Rolling out token changes could cause visual drift in dashboards if consumers relied on implicit spacing; include migration plan and toggle
comments: 2026-02-22 — Aisha: Kicked off initial exploration. Built two low-fidelity prototypes (canvas overlay vs direct DOM). Canvas looks promising to reduce reflow.
2026-02-25 — UX Research: Proposed rapid unmoderated test to validate discoverability of density spectrum UI before high-fidelity work.
2026-03-01 — Liam: Engineering spike complete. Canvas overlay reduces layout thrash in Chrome; Safari needs small compositor hint. Captured flamegraphs and added to ENG-1984.
2026-03-04 — Miguel (Accessibility Review): Suggest minimizing aria-live updates during drag; recommend announcing final width only. Also requested keyboard hint in tooltip.
2026-03-08 — PM (Rina Singh): Reviewed and approved trade-offs. Request: include opt-in immediate-apply prop for embedded dashboards where consumers already expect live resizing.
2026-03-10 — Aisha: Updated acceptance criteria to require telemetry events. Added migration guidance link placeholder. Moving to In Progress.
